title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Karachi. Tip #1
body: Sit outside KGS or Nixor at two o'clock and you've read the city. If a Land Cruiser pulls up with a guard in front and the driver already has the door, that's the tier. If a sixteen-year-old drives himself down Khayaban-e-Shamsheer with no licence and no concern, that's a family that has never had a problem a phone call couldn't solve. It's a sealed deal if the gate opens before the car reaches it.
caption:
Tip #1 😭 "I'll ask the driver" is the whole city.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Karachi. Tip #2
body: Karachi rich kids have a coast and Lahore doesn't, and they will remind you. Sandspit, Hawksbay, French Beach, and the hut is somebody's family's since the eighties. Nobody books anything, somebody just says the word and eleven people appear. It's a sealed deal if there's a photo of the same group at the same hut every year since they were nine.
caption:
Tip #2 😭 "I'll ask the driver" is the whole city.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Karachi. Tip #3
body: Listen for the driver in every plan. "I'll ask the driver" is the most Karachi sentence there is, because nobody in this tier fights that traffic themselves. The car is status, the driver is logistics, both are assumed. It's a sealed deal if a teenager's WhatsApp thread with the driver is longer than the one with their father.
caption:
Tip #3 😭 "I'll ask the driver" is the whole city.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Karachi. Tip #4
body: Ask where they eat and the answer is a commercial, not a restaurant. "Khadda Market," "Bukhari," "Badar," and they'll assume you know which one. Do Darya when relatives visit. Boat Basin at two in the morning. It's a sealed deal if they've ordered the same thing at the same place since school and the man there starts making it on sight.
caption:
Tip #4 😭 "I'll ask the driver" is the whole city.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Karachi. Tip #5
body: Ask about university and the plan is already closed. "IBA, probably" is the version for relatives. LUMS means Lahore and a hostel and an argument settled two years ago. Abroad was decided when the kid was fourteen. It's a sealed deal if a Common App deadline caused more stress in that house than any board exam.

Tip #5 😭 "I'll ask the driver" is the whole city.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Karachi. Tip #6
body: Watch how they talk about Lahore, it's a whole personality. Karachi thinks Lahore is slow, pretty, and slightly fake. Lahore thinks Karachi is rude and exhausting. Both are right and neither will concede an inch. It's a sealed deal if they've been to Lahore for four weddings and still say they could never live there.

Tip #6 😭 "I'll ask the driver" is the whole city.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Karachi. Tip #7
body: Ask about the power and the water, then watch nothing happen. K-Electric goes, the generator catches in two seconds, the conversation continues. The tanker has never once been mentioned in that house. That's the actual privilege and it's invisible from inside. It's a sealed deal if a teenager cannot tell you what a unit of electricity costs.

Tip #7 😭 "I'll ask the driver" is the whole city.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Karachi. Tip #8
body: Ask what they do in Ramadan, because Karachi does this better than anywhere. Sehri at Burns Road or a dhaba at three in the morning, twenty people, cars parked badly, genuinely the best social window of the year. Money doesn't change this one, which is why everyone remembers it. It's a sealed deal if the same group has done the same sehri spot every year since school.
